lesson.title: Kubernetes from Zero, part 22: troubleshooting Services, DNS, stuck deletes and sick nodes
lesson.description: Fix a Service with no endpoints, a DNS lookup that fails, an object stuck in Terminating, a NotReady node and an evicted Pod, then debug with kubectl debug.
lesson.tested: Broke and fixed each case on a two-node kind v0.33.0 cluster, node v1.37.0, kubectl v1.37.2, 10 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: Most failures outside the Pod are a mismatch you can read from the API: a selector with no endpoints, a name in the wrong namespace, a finalizer nobody owns, or a node that stopped reporting.

cheatsheet.intro: Services, DNS, finalizers, nodes, and the commands from Lesson 22.

rows.name: No endpoints
rows.role: The Service exists and has a ClusterIP, and the EndpointSlice is empty. The lab's selector was the typo wbe.

rows.name: Wrong port
rows.role: Endpoints were present and wget still said Connection refused. The slice showed port 8080. The container listened on 80.

rows.name: DNS
rows.role: bad address means the name did not resolve. web.default looks in the default namespace. The full name is service.namespace.svc.cluster.local.

rows.name: Finalizer
rows.role: An object, or a whole namespace, stays Terminating until the owner removes the finalizer. The lab's key was example.com/cleanup.

rows.name: NotReady
rows.role: The lab's node went NotReady 49 seconds after kubelet stopped. EndpointSlice ready became false while Pods still showed Running. Eviction followed the 300 second toleration.

rows.name: Evicted
rows.role: kind sets node disk thresholds to 0 percent, so the lab could not show DiskPressure. A Pod with an ephemeral-storage limit of 20Mi was evicted when it wrote past that limit.

rows.name: No shell
rows.role: kubectl debug --target adds an ephemeral container beside a container that has no shell. debug node starts a Pod with the node root at /host.

rows.name: kube-proxy
rows.role: The first wget after the targetPort patch still failed, and the same command three seconds later worked.

rows.name: Namespace
rows.role: A stuck namespace reports NamespaceContentRemaining and NamespaceFinalizersRemaining, and names the finalizer.

items.what: Follow the request in order: name, endpoints, port, Pod. Connection refused and bad address are different stops.
Stopping kubelet made the worker NotReady. Replacements stayed Pending with an untolerated taint until kubelet started again.
status.reason said Evicted: Pod ephemeral local storage usage exceeds the total limit of containers 20Mi. Failed Pods stay until you delete them.
kubectl debug node/k8s-ep22-worker ran chroot /host. On kind that worked. The docs say it fails without privilege, and the lesson points at --profile=sysadmin.

commands.note: empty means the selector matches nothing
compare the selector with pod labels

commands.cmd: kubectl exec -n k8s-from-zero client -- nslookup web.k8s-from-zero.svc.cluster.local
kubectl get configmap stuck -n k8s-from-zero -o jsonpath='{.metadata.deletionTimestamp}{"  "}{.metadata.finalizers}{"\n"}'
kubectl get pod disk-hog -n k8s-from-zero -o jsonpath='{.status.phase} {.status.reason}: {.status.message}{"\n"}'
kubectl debug node/k8s-ep22-worker -n k8s-from-zero --image=busybox:1.37 -- chroot /host sh -c 'systemctl is-active kubelet'

homework.intro: Use a kind cluster with one worker and the namespace k8s-from-zero. The lesson's cluster is k8s-ep22. Answers are in the separate answer key.

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: What is the difference between bad address and Connection refused?
exercises.a: bad address means the name did not resolve. Connection refused means the name resolved and nothing answered. A wrong namespace gives the first. A wrong targetPort gives the second, even when endpoints exist.

exercises.q: Why does an object stay in Terminating after kubectl delete returns?
exercises.a: A finalizer is still set. The owner is supposed to remove it. The lab's ConfigMap kept example.com/cleanup, and deletionTimestamp was set, until a patch cleared the finalizers.

exercises.q: How soon did the lab's node go NotReady, and when were its Pods evicted?
exercises.a: NotReady 49 seconds after kubelet stopped. The default toleration for not-ready and unreachable is 300 seconds, and the eviction came after that. EndpointSlice ready was already false while get pods still said Running.

exercises.q: With the lesson's typo selector, what does the EndpointSlice show, and what does wget from the client print?
exercises.a: No addresses. wget says Connection refused to the ClusterIP. After the selector is patched to app.kubernetes.io/name=web, endpoints appear. If PORTS is still 8080, the Pod on port 80 still refuses the Service.

exercises.q: Scale CoreDNS to 0 and look up the Service. What did the lesson record?
exercises.a: The kube-dns EndpointSlice has no endpoints. wget to web.k8s-from-zero prints bad address. nslookup to the full name times out and says connection refused to 10.96.0.10. Scaling CoreDNS back to 2 restores the lookup.

exercises.q: Read disk-hog's status.reason. What message did the lesson record, and why was this not DiskPressure?
exercises.a: Evicted: Pod ephemeral local storage usage exceeds the total limit of containers 20Mi. kind sets the node disk thresholds to 0 percent, so the lab could not raise DiskPressure. Evicted Pods stay Failed until you delete them.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: Write your prediction first. Then check the answer key.

exercises.q: You patch targetPort and the next wget still fails. What does the lesson tell you to do before you undo the fix?
exercises.a: Wait a second. The first try after the patch still got Connection refused, and the same command three seconds later worked, because kube-proxy had not programmed the node yet.

exercises.q: A namespace stays Terminating. Which conditions does the lesson name?
exercises.a: NamespaceContentRemaining and NamespaceFinalizersRemaining. The message names the finalizer and how many objects still hold it. Clear that finalizer only when you know nothing else will.

exercises.q: kubectl exec into a pause Pod fails. What does the lesson use instead?
exercises.a: kubectl debug with --target and an image that has a shell, for one container. kubectl debug node/NAME for the node, with the node root at /host. Delete the debug Pod when you are done.
